meta.originalInput: Every time you postpone uncomfortable work, you aren't just losing time—you're rewiring your brain to make quitting automatic. Delaying a task triggers an immediate drop in stress hormones. Your brain misinterprets this sudden relief as survival, cementing a dopamine reward loop for avoidance. The more you delay, the deeper this neural pathway carves into your habits. To break the cycle, decouple the task from anxiety. Shrink your starting threshold to just ninety seconds of friction. Lower the perceived threat, and the urge to flee evaporates.
